html:
The Kebra Nagast, "The Glory of the Kings", is a 14th-century epic in Ge'ez, the church language of Ethiopia. It traces the kings of Ethiopia back to King Solomon of Israel and the Queen of Sheba.

In its story the queen, called Makeda, visits Solomon in Jerusalem and bears his son, Menelik I. When Menelik grows up he visits his father and brings the Ark of the Covenant back to Ethiopia, so that God's favour passes from Israel to the Ethiopians. The book mixes the Bible, Jewish and Christian legend and Ethiopian tradition, and says it was translated from Arabic.

It was written soon after the Solomonic dynasty took power in 1270 from the Zagwe kings, and it gave the new line a sacred right to rule. Every emperor down to Haile Selassie, deposed in 1974, claimed descent from Solomon. The story also shapes Rastafari belief, and the Ethiopian church still holds that the Ark is kept at Aksum.
sum: The Kebra Nagast, "The Glory of the Kings", is a 14th-century epic in Ge'ez, the church language of Ethiopia. It traces the kings of Ethiopia back to King Solomon of Israel and the Queen of Sheba.
